title: Taiwan Can’t Fight Beijing’s History War While Erasing Its Own ROC Legacy
gist: At the Trump-Xi summit the White House called the US and China WWII allies who 'fought side by side', omitting that the Republic of China, not the PRC (founded 1949), fought Japan. Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council and Deputy Foreign Minister Wu Chih-chung protested this framing as 'de-ROC-ization' that lets the Chinese Communist Party replace the ROC in history.

themes.theme: White House 'side by side' WWII wording

insights.claim: At the Trump-Xi summit, the White House described the United States and China as World War II allies who 'fought side by side to win the war', collapsing the Republic of China and the People’s Republic of China into one unbroken 'China'.
insights.so_what: Washington adopting Beijing-friendly historical language in summit communications is a soft signal of US accommodation toward the PRC that matters for Taiwan's standing.
insights.quote: It was a small phrase with a large omission.
insights.locator: At last week’s summit between U.S.
insights.speaker: Ivan I-Wei Huang

insights.claim: The PRC did not exist until 1949, four years after Japan's surrender; the government that represented China and fought alongside the US against Japan was the Republic of China, so the summit language risked letting the PRC inherit the legacy of a war it did not fight.
insights.so_what: Historical-legitimacy narratives are part of Beijing's sovereignty claims over Taiwan; US endorsement of them weakens the ROC's distinct international identity.
insights.quote: risked allowing the PRC to inherit the legacy of a war it did not fight
insights.locator: At last week’s summit between U.S.
insights.speaker: Ivan I-Wei Huang

insights.claim: Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council insisted the ROC was the 'true ally' that fought with the US in WWII and stressed the PRC did not exist during the war.
insights.so_what: Taipei is publicly contesting US wording, showing sensitivity to any drift in Washington's framing after a Trump-Xi summit.
insights.speaker: Ivan I-Wei Huang

insights.claim: Taiwan's Deputy Foreign Minister Wu Chih-chung called the framing an act of 'de-ROC-ization', in which the Republic of China's existence is erased from history and replaced by the Chinese Communist Party.
insights.so_what: Taiwanese officials view historical erasure as a strategic threat tied to Beijing's broader 'history war' over sovereignty.
insights.quote: calling the framing an act of “de-ROC-ization”
